lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: deciding whether a model is consistent with data
lessonRef.title: Concept model C: deciding whether a model is consistent with data

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example is written more briefly. Fill in the reasoning it leaves out.

items.prompt: Mean 100, sd 15. What percentage lies between 70 and 130?

steps: That is 100 ± 30, which is two standard deviations.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A researcher runs a sample survey with randomly selected participants. What kind of conclusion does this design support?
choices: It supports generalising from the sample to the population, but not a causal claim.
It supports both generalisation and causation, provided the sample is large.
It supports neither generalisation nor causation, because self-selection can bias both.
It supports a causal conclusion about the treatment, within the population studied.

items.prompt: A random sample of 625 people gives a sample proportion of 67%. Using the conservative margin of error 1/√n, give the approximate margin of error and the resulting interval.
choices: ±67%, giving 0% to 134%
±4%, giving 63% to 71%
±8%, giving 59% to 75%

items.prompt: In 1000 simulations under the assumption of no difference, 22 produced a result at least as extreme as the one observed. What should be concluded?
choices: The simulation proves that the observed difference is real.
The observed result is not statistically significant: it occurred in 2.2% of simulations, which is not unusual.
The simulation proves that there is no difference.
The observed result is statistically significant: it occurred in only 2.2% of simulations, below the usual 5% threshold.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A quantity is approximately normal with mean 64 and standard deviation 7. Approximately what percentage of values lie between 50 and 78?
choices: about 50%
about 68%
about 95%
about 99.7%

items.prompt: A researcher runs an observational study of volunteers who chose their own group. What kind of conclusion does this design support?
choices: It supports neither generalisation nor causation, because self-selection can bias both.
It supports generalising from the sample to the population, but not a causal claim.
It supports a causal conclusion about the treatment, within the population studied.
It supports both generalisation and causation, provided the sample is large.

items.prompt: A random sample of 100 people gives a sample proportion of 49%. Using the conservative margin of error 1/√n, give the approximate margin of error and the resulting interval.
choices: ±1%, giving 48% to 50%
±20%, giving 29% to 69%
±10%, giving 39% to 59%
±49%, giving 0% to 98%

items.prompt: In 1000 simulations under the assumption of no difference, 28 produced a result at least as extreme as the one observed. What should be concluded?
choices: The observed result is statistically significant: it occurred in only 2.8% of simulations, below the usual 5% threshold.
The observed result is not statistically significant: it occurred in 2.8% of simulations, which is not unusual.
The simulation proves that the observed difference is real.
The simulation proves that there is no difference.

items.prompt: A quantity is approximately normal with mean 178 and standard deviation 4. Approximately what percentage of values lie between 166 and 190?
choices: about 50%
about 99.7%
about 68%
about 95%

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: A researcher runs a randomised controlled experiment with participants randomly assigned to treatments. What kind of conclusion does this design support?
choices: It supports a causal conclusion about the treatment, within the population studied.
It supports neither generalisation nor causation, because self-selection can bias both.
It supports generalising from the sample to the population, but not a causal claim.
It supports both generalisation and causation, provided the sample is large.

items.prompt: A random sample of 100 people gives a sample proportion of 39%. Using the conservative margin of error 1/√n, give the approximate margin of error and the resulting interval.
choices: ±1%, giving 38% to 40%
±20%, giving 19% to 59%
±39%, giving 0% to 78%
±10%, giving 29% to 49%
